title: 4 out of 5 toddler foods are ultraprocessed. Nearly half fail to meet nutrition standards
facts: A study of over 2,700 toddler foods in the US found more than 80% are ultraprocessed.
Nearly half of analyzed US toddler food products failed to meet at least one World Health Organization nutritional benchmark.
Erin Hudson is a postdoctoral researcher at Children's Hospital Los Angeles.
Erin Hudson presented the toddler nutrition study at the annual meeting of the American Society for Nutrition.
Almost 25% of analyzed toddler foods exceeded recommended sodium levels.
Jane Houlihan serves as research director for the organization Healthy Babies Bright Futures.
The American Academy of Pediatrics identifies the first 1,000 days of life as critical for child brain development.
Marissa Burgermaster is an assistant professor of nutritional sciences at the University of Texas at Austin.
The US Food and Drug Administration proposed a front-of-package nutrition rating system for packaged foods in 2025.
Researchers evaluated 2,783 toddler food products purchased across 21 grocery stores in Austin, Texas.
The NOVA food classification system categorizes foods into four distinct tiers based on processing levels.
A January study found over 70% of 651 baby and toddler foods contained additives linked to gut inflammation.
Elizabeth Dunford is an adjunct assistant professor of nutrition at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.
WHO guidelines advise against added sugar and artificial sweeteners in foods for children aged 6 to 36 months.
The Consumer Brands Association represents packaged food manufacturers in the United States.
